Chewy oat and raisin cookies

by Ana Ruiz

These are the cookies my grandmother kept in a biscuit tin on top of the fridge, chewy in the middle and just crisp enough at the edges to snap.

The trick is to chill the dough for an hour before baking. Cold butter melts more slowly in the oven, so the cookies hold their shape instead of spreading into one flat sheet.

Soak the raisins in hot tea for ten minutes first and they stay plump rather than turning into little burnt pebbles on the tray.
